text:
Jamie: quick sync — I ran a token-level profile across the /chat/completions route and we have a regression around KV cache access. per-token latency jumped ~25% on average starting 1754950000, bigger variance on long contexts. attaching a couple trace ids below.

Alex: can you paste the sample traces? is it KV miss or hit time going up?

Jamie: trace links: https://traces.redwood.local/trace/tr-9f8a7c and https://traces.redwood.local/trace/tr-9f8b01. 
Stack excerpt: ```
stage: decode -> kernel_launch -> kv_lookup -> kv_deserialize -> attention
latencies_ms: [0.9, 2.1, 8.6, 1.0, 6.2]
kv_hit: true
```

Maria: looks like kv_lookup is the outlier (8.6ms). Could be serialization path on recent kernel change. Were any kernel selection heuristics rolled out? @Tanner? :thinking_face:

Tanner: I rolled a small kernel selector tweak last week (1754920000) that prioritizes FP16-packed kernels for some layers. It should be orthogonal but might change memory layout for KV pages. My rollout note: "fallback to generic kernel when packed layout mismatch" but we may be falling into a slow path.

Jamie: yep that matches timing. We should correlate request-level metrics -> trace spans -> prom metrics. Right now dashboards show only per-route p50/p95 token latency aggregated, not token-stage breakdown by trace id.

Alex: two problems: 1) metrics label cardinality if we tag by trace_id/token_index, 2) sampling: we can't record every token stage for every request. Propose: store per-request breakdown as a short JSON blob in trace baggage, then surface top-N in dashboard. That avoids high-cardinality time-series.

Maria: agree. We already emit token_latency_bucket{stage="kv_lookup",route="/chat/completions"} histograms. But no trace join key visible in the dashboard. If we add a metric label trace_id we explode series. Instead, add a span tag "rid" and a trace annotation with small JSON: {"token_stages": ["kv:8.6","attn:6.2"], "sample_rate": 0.01}. Dashboards can pull sample traces and compute sample-level breakdowns.

Tanner: implementation notes: runtime can attach trace_rid in the request context. For private deployments we'll need to honor PII rules (strip full prompt). This is fine if we only emit stage durations numeric arrays.

SRE-Oncall: also consider adding an aggregated metric: token_stage_p50_ms_by_route{stage,route} populated from sampled traces via a job. That gives low-cardinality SLO metrics.

Jamie: plan suggestion: 1) add lightweight trace annotation + rid in next runtime patch (Tanner), 2) add sampler in edge router to tag 1% of requests for full token-stage collection (Alex), 3) add a nightly job to ingest sampled traces and emit aggregated per-route stage p50/p95 metrics (Maria), 4) build per-request breakdown panel in Console that links spike bars to sampled trace IDs (Dashboard team).

Alex: small proto for trace annotation payload: ```json
{"rid":"r-1755abcd","token_stages_ms":[0.9,2.1,8.6,1.0,6.2],"stages":["decode","kernel_launch","kv_lookup","kv_deserialize","attention"],"sample_rate":0.01}
```
This stays in tracing DB, not metrics store. Aggregator job converts to metrics.

Maria: question: how to handle KV cache hits vs misses in the visualization? Need a separate series with hit_rate label. We should emit a sampled boolean and then aggregator calculates hit_rate and hit_latency separately.

Jamie: agreed. Add field "kv_hit_mask": [1,1,1] or simply count hits.

infra-bot: deploy scheduled: runtime/kernel-selector v2.3.1 -> canary on infra-canary at 1755020000. See https://ci.redwood.local/builds/3212 :robot_face:

Tanner: I'll hold the rollout until we have the sampler + trace annotation in canary. won't promote until we validate no slow path on KV.

SRE-Oncall: for dashboards, we need three things: token-stage stacked bars (p50/p95), per-route SLO lines, and a link column to sampled trace IDs. UX note: keep default sample window 1h to avoid noise.

Jamie: assigning owners: Tanner (runtime annotation & kernel fallback audit), Alex (edge sampler + trace payload schema), Maria (aggregator job + metrics mapping + dashboard panels). I'll add tickets and 1755 retro notes. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

Alex: quick follow-up — for the aggregator job, should we use batch job reading from traces or a streaming consumer from tracing-exporter? streaming might reduce latency for alerts.

Maria: streaming is better for near-real-time alerting but more infra. start with batch hourly, iterate to streaming if alerts lag.

Jamie: ok hitting sync closure. If anyone finds other noisy kernels, drop traces here.
